Code Design

Source: CODE_DESIGN.md

How bcgwcat2 is put together, for anyone (human or AI agent) working on the code. For installing and using the package, see the README.

Overview

bcgwcat2 is an R package (Province of British Columbia) for working with groundwater chemistry data from EnMoDS (Environmental Monitoring Data System). It is a rewrite of bcgwcat, which used the older EMS system, and is still in early, experimental development.

All data access goes through the renmods package (installed from GitHub; see Remotes in DESCRIPTION).

Resources

Learn more about EnMoDS data here: https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/environment/research-monitoring-reporting/monitoring/environmental-monitoring-data-system

In particular see the Reference lists section including the relevant files:

  • All observed properties
  • Data classifications
  • Detection conditions
  • Mediums
  • Observed properties and analytical methods
  • QC Type
  • Units

Development workflow

Run from R in the package root:

devtools::load_all() # load package for interactive work
devtools::document() # regenerate man/ and NAMESPACE from roxygen
devtools::check()
devtools::build_readme() # README.md is generated from README.Rmd
bcgwcat_app() # launch the full Shiny app (port 7405)
test_mod("overview") # launch one Shiny module on its own (internal, R/tests.R)
source("data-raw/parameters.R") # rebuild lookup tables (needs network access)
  • NAMESPACE and man/ are generated by roxygen, so don’t edit them by hand.
  • Edit README.Rmd, not README.md.
  • Code is formatted with Air (air.toml: 80-character lines, 2-space indent, <- assignment). Run air format ..
  • RELEASE.R has the release checklist. DEVTESTS.R holds scratch code for manual exploration.

Tests: run with devtools::test(), or run one file with devtools::test(filter = "format"). Tests that read EnMoDS data use the local renmods cache, so they are skipped on CRAN and CI. The old test suite is in NEXT/tests/, which is excluded from the build and hasn’t been ported yet.

Data pipeline

The core of the package doesn’t depend on Shiny. Data flows through these steps:

  1. fetch_renmods() (R/fetch.R) connects through renmods::renmods_connect(), filters by Location_ID (EMS IDs, always converted to character) and by date range, then loads the result into memory. It returns the raw EnMoDS columns, which have TitleCase names.
  2. fmt_minimal() (R/format.R) is the central formatter, and almost everything downstream expects its output. It selects columns, converts names to lower case and keeps only known parameters. It then runs add_obs_wells() → add_bcgwcat_params() → add_meq() → add_placeholder() → add_charge_balance() → add_water_type().
    • The output is in long format: one row per location, date and parameter.
    • Derived values are added as extra rows. These include meq values (result_unit == "meq/l"), charge balance and anion/cation sums.
  3. fmt_wide() pivots the output of fmt_minimal() to wide format. Before pivoting, it resolves repeated and multi-method measurements with fix_multiple_measures() (R/fix.R).
  4. Calculations and outputs:
    • meq(), charge_balance() and water_type() are in R/calculations.R.
    • Comparison with water quality guidelines is in R/water_quality.R.
    • stiff_plot() is in R/plots.R.
    • The reactable tables are in R/tables.R.

check_samples() (R/checks.R) validates inputs. If it receives raw output from fetch_renmods(), it applies fmt_minimal() automatically.

Data assumptions

  • A sample is considered an observation with a unique Location_ID, Observed_Date_Time, Observed_Parameter_ID, QC_Type, and (possibly) Data_Classification

Parameter and metadata lookup tables

CSV lookup tables in inst/extdata/ control how parameters and columns are named. They are read at runtime by read_data() (R/utils-data.R) and exposed through index_params(), index_meta(), index_meta_params(), ion_details() and wq_std().

  • index_params() maps EnMoDS parameter names (enmods_param) to snake_case bcgwcat_param names. The code uses bcgwcat_param names throughout.
  • index_meta() and index_meta_params() map column names between EnMoDS and bcgwcat.
  • meta_vars(which, param_vars) returns the set of columns for "bcgwcat" or "enmods". These columns are also the keys that identify a single observation.
  • EnMoDS reports its own charge balance and ion sums. Those parameters get an _enmods suffix, so they don’t clash with the charge_balance, anion_sum and cation_sum that this package calculates.

These CSVs are generated files. data-raw/parameters.R builds them from:

  • the hand-edited CSVs in data-raw/
  • the ion_details table, which is defined inside the script
  • the drinking water guidelines (wq_std), which are downloaded with bcdata

To change a table, edit the source in data-raw/ and re-run the script. Don’t edit inst/extdata/ directly. The script also writes the internal objects ems_ids_all and min_date to R/sysdata.rda.

Shiny app

bcgwcat_app() (R/app.R) builds a bslib::page_navbar from modules in R/mod_*.R. Each module has a mod_<name>_ui() and a mod_<name>_server() function.

  • Overview: mod_overview_server() handles the status and downloads of the renmods cache. It returns updated, a reactiveVal counter that goes up each time the local data changes.
  • Data: mod_data_server(updated, ...) takes that counter and handles choosing EMS IDs and dates and fetching the data.
  • Water quality and plots: the data module returns the sample data that mod_water_quality_server() and mod_plots_server() use.
  • Messages: the package’s inform() and abort() (cli wrappers in R/messages.R) are shown in the in-app console through with_messages() (R/utils-shiny.R).
  • Theme: the theme comes from inst/shiny-assets/_brand.yml, and the BC Sans fonts are bundled.
  • Prompts: bcgwcat_ui() sets rlang_interactive = FALSE, so renmods doesn’t stop to ask questions in the terminal.

Work in progress

NEXT/ is excluded from the build. It holds features that will be ported into the package: ggplot piper plots, the old tests and the vignettes.

Conventions

  • In dplyr code, use the .data$ and .env$ pronouns.
  • Namespace-qualify function calls (dplyr::, tidyr::, …). The exceptions are shiny and bslib, which are imported whole, and glue.
  • Use the package’s own inform() and abort() for messages and errors.
  • New R files start with the Province of BC Apache 2.0 copyright header.
